name: Ghana
summary: Red, gold and green horizontal bands with a black five-pointed star in the centre. Designed by Theodosia Okoh for independence in 1957, it was the second African flag (after Ethiopia's) to use red, gold and green and helped make them the Pan-African colours.
origin: Ghana, formerly the Gold Coast, was the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence, on 6 March 1957. Theodosia Okoh, a teacher and artist, designed the flag.

From 1964 to 1966, under Kwame Nkrumah's one-party state, the gold band was replaced with white to match the ruling Convention People's Party's colours. The original design was restored in 1966 after Nkrumah was overthrown.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of those who died in the struggle for independence.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The country's mineral wealth; the colony's name was the Gold Coast.

symbols.name: Black Star
symbols.description: A black five-pointed star in the gold band.
symbols.meaning: African freedom and emancipation; the 'lodestar of African freedom'. It recalls Marcus Garvey's Black Star Line shipping company.

history.label: Gold Coast colony
history.note: Blue ensign with an elephant badge.

history.label: One-party state
history.note: White band in place of gold.

facts: Ghana's national football team is nicknamed the Black Stars after the flag.
Bolivia and Lithuania use red, yellow and green horizontal bands in different orders.
Guinea-Bissau, Togo, Senegal and others later adopted red, gold and green with a black star.
clues: Red, gold and green horizontal bands with a black star in the middle.
Its star gives a national football team its nickname.
The first flag of an independent sub-Saharan African colony, from 1957.
For two years its middle band was white under a one-party state.
